claims.supporting_snippet: Select a cell within your data. Select Home > Format as Table. Choose a style for your table. In the Create Table dialog box, set your cell range. Mark if your table has headers. Select OK .
claims.text: Select a cell within your data, then select Home > Format as Table, choose a style, set the cell range in the Create Table dialog box, mark if your table has headers, and select OK.

claims.supporting_snippet: Simple formulas always start with an equal sign ( = ), followed by constants that are numeric values and calculation operators such as plus ( + ), minus ( - ), asterisk( * ), or forward slash ( / ) signs.
claims.text: Simple formulas always start with an equal sign (=), followed by constants that are numeric values and calculation operators such as plus (+), minus (-), asterisk(*), or forward slash (/) signs.

claims.supporting_snippet: To add a blank table, select the cells you want included in the table and click Insert > Table .
claims.text: To add a blank table, select the cells you want included in the table and click Insert > Table.

claims.supporting_snippet: You can enter as many constants and operators in a formula as you need, up to 8192 characters.
claims.text: You can enter as many constants and operators in a formula as you need, up to 8192 characters.

claims.supporting_snippet: If you don't check the My table has headers box, Excel for the web adds headers with default names like Column1 and Column2 above the data.
